root_adjudication.tannase_green_tea: One BTC enzyme-treated extract preparation. Selected efficacy population 33/34 from 80 randomized. Nominal right-flexor change and right-grip relative-preservation results; remaining strength and every comparative mass result null. SPPB results missing. No stated hierarchy/multiplicity adjustment. Baseline exclusions, lower active right-flexor baseline, Table 3 unit omission, Table 1 impossible pooled means and conditional myostatin-P inconsistency retained. No isolated epicatechin, gallic acid, ordinary-tea or other product inheritance.
root_adjudication.riboflavin: One parallel concurrent comparison allocated alternately by arrival, without documented random sequence. Selected 32 complete-data finishers from 44 starters, eight baseline runners. Day 3/5 400 m signal with null group-by-time interaction does not establish equal-baseline recovery acceleration. Overall soreness null; restricted analysis exploratory. Retain preparation/adherence, medication discrepancy and missing baseline/ITT limits. Existing disease-specific metabolic findings remain separate.
root_adjudication.coq10: One 17-person three-condition crossover at partial original-text exposure depth. Retain 300 mg cycling-change and post-task-fatigue positives, 100 mg performance nonpositive finding and recovery trend only. Native quantitative estimates and notice contents remain UNKNOWN. Four-week test spacing is not verified drug-free washout. No complete-main credit.

design.model: Human, trained and experienced WSER ultramarathon runners; no selected neuromuscular, MADD or BUB1B population.
design.allocation_actual: Alternating assignment by arrival order at race registration, not documented random sequence; quasi-random/nonrandom alternating allocation.

allocation_source.literal_anchor: in an alternating fashion based on the order of arrival

design.blinding: Subjects and on-site researchers reported blind; details of sequence construction and concealment beyond on-site blinding are not supplied.
design.race_context: 2016 WSER 161.3 km, 5500 m climb/7000 m descent, ambient 1–34 C; analyzed group mean finish times approximately 27 hours.
design.endpoint_hierarchy: Soreness and 400-m run time are both called main outcome variables. Sample size was based on a 1.5-point soreness difference; no preregistered primary/secondary hierarchy was identified.

statistics.functional_soreness: Two-way group-by-time repeated-measures ANOVA and Bonferroni post-tests.
statistics.power_plan: 13 per group for a 1.5-point soreness difference, common SD 1.5 and 80% power; target minimum 17 per group allowing 25–30% attrition.

preparation.active: Investigator-prepared capsules containing 100 mg riboflavin from Nature’s Way Products, Inc.; no riboflavin-5-phosphate or B-vitamin mixture specified.
preparation.active_nominal_schedule: 100 mg orally with water 0.5–1 h before start and 100 mg at the 90-km aid station, observed ingestion; planned 200 mg total.
preparation.active_timing: Discussion estimates second dose 11–16 h after first during a 20–30 h race.
preparation.active_missing: Lot, purity, chemical form beyond riboflavin, excipients and actual systemic exposure not reported.
preparation.comparator: 95 mg maltodextrin (Now) plus 5 mg of 10% beta-carotene powder (BulkSupplements.com) per capsule; two capsules on the same schedule.

comparator_beta_carotene_calculation.kind: Derived nominal estimate from 5 mg powder x 10%; not measured content or bioavailability.

preparation.attribution_limit: Riboflavin capsule versus this maltodextrin/beta-carotene comparator. Authors acknowledge antioxidant beta-carotene but assume a negligible effect at this low dose; comparator inertness was not demonstrated.
preparation.adherence: One placebo subject missed the 90-km capsule; two riboflavin subjects vomited within 1 h after that capsule. Analysis/exclusion handling and absorbed doses are unclear.

material_limits: Alternating arrival-order allocation lacks a documented random sequence and robust concealment.
Only 8/32 complete participants had baseline 400-m times; between-arm baseline fitness is unknown.
400-m group-by-time P=.60: a post-race group speed difference does not demonstrate a differential recovery rate.
Overall soreness group P=.14 and interaction P=.25 were null; P=.043 restricted analysis was explicitly exploratory.
Completer/finisher selection and unequal follow-up losses; no intention-to-treat functional result.

Self-timed unsupervised tests; effort, site, environment and repeated-test learning were not controlled. In the eight baseline runners, pooled trial 2 was faster than trial 1, but learning was not formally tested.
Pain-medication avoidance was not followed: Table 1 reports during-race 50%/36%, post-race 33%/43%. Observational null comparisons cannot exclude confounding.
Dietary antioxidant intake was not measured; later post-race exercise and other recovery modalities were incompletely quantified.
Figure means/SD lack numerical effect sizes and confidence intervals; original participant data were not publicly posted, so exact contrasts and robust reanalysis remain pending.
Two active subjects vomited after the 90-km dose and one placebo subject missed that dose; absorbed dose and analysis handling are unclear.
CK was null and mitochondrial/oxidative mediation was not measured. Proposed mechanisms remain hypotheses.
